proof_summary: Lucas congruences split each sum at indices of the form \(p+r\): the middle binomial terms vanish modulo \(p\) and the low and high terms cancel in pairs, while at \(p-1\) one gets \(a(p-1)=1\) and, for \(c\), only \(k=(p-1)/2\) survives, giving \(c(p-1)=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Thus both Hankel matrices are anti-triangular modulo \(p\); reversing the rows makes them triangular, and combining the reversal sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) with the respective constant anti-diagonal entries yields the two determinant congruences.
